title: Financial Derivatives and Risk Management
subtitle: Contracts, replication, and the limits of a hedge

chapters.title: What a derivative changes: cash flows, exposure, and risk
objectives: Build a dated, signed cash-flow model for forwards, options, and swaps
Distinguish a hedge identity from a forecast and a payoff from financed profit
Explain why clearing and margin mitigate credit risk while creating liquidity demands
State a precise finite-state no-arbitrage test
chapters.prerequisites: Algebra, elementary probability, and present value. Finance terminology is defined locally.
chapters.source_scope: Full English NPTEL Official caption track read sequentially; no comprehensive slide or audio audit. Examples and formal finite-state constructions are original additions.

chapters.title: Forward prices come from financed replication
objectives: Construct both cash-and-carry arbitrage directions with dated financing
Separate an existing forward's value from its delivery quotation
Derive income, storage and currency adjustments with explicit units
Explain why consumption assets can defeat reverse carry
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 1 cash-flow signs, elementary exponentials and present value. All financing conventions are stated locally.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions read sequentially for positions 3–5; no comprehensive audiovisual audit. MIT forward-pricing slides 17–22 inspected.

chapters.title: Futures redistribute cash flows through time
objectives: Build a daily variation-settlement and collateral ledger
Separate notional exposure, margin deposits and trading profit
Derive deterministic-rate forward/futures equivalence by a feasible strategy
Explain residual clearing and funding risks
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 1–2 dated cash flows, compounding and statewise replication. Pricing-probability preview is clearly marked.
chapters.source_scope: Full English captions read sequentially for positions 6–8. Selected BIS PFMI and MIT forward/futures material inspected; no comprehensive audiovisual or current-exchange-rule audit.

chapters.title: Exposure, hedge direction, and the basis that remains
objectives: Define a statistical exposure with the correct units and horizon
Derive OLS orthogonality and identify residual nonlinear risk
Build long and short hedge cash flows using a fixed basis convention
Compare contract choices by their combined risk rather than hoped-for gains
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 1–3 cash-flow accounting; elementary means, variances and differentiation, developed locally where used.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential English caption reading for positions 9–11; no comprehensive audiovisual audit. Philosophical digression treated as contextual rather than a financial theorem.

chapters.title: Hedge size is a covariance projection with trading units
objectives: Derive minimum-variance sizing with explicit exposure and contract units
Prove the squared-correlation residual-risk formula
Compute the exact variance cost of integer rounding
Diagnose cross-hedge and estimation-regime failures
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 4 covariance, OLS projection and hedge directions; scalar differentiation and finite second moments.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential English captions for positions 12–13. NIST least-squares definition and limitations inspected. Synthetic examples independently executed.

chapters.title: Portfolio risk depends on covariance; priced risk requires a model
objectives: Derive portfolio moments and globally certified two-asset and many-asset variance minima
Separate efficient-frontier optimization from equilibrium pricing
Derive CAPM from an interior Sharpe-ratio condition
State the assumptions behind residual diversification
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 5 covariance projection; finite second moments, differentiation and elementary matrix notation.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential English captions for positions 14–16; selected MIT portfolio and CAPM teaching passages inspected. Synthetic moment calculations executed.

chapters.title: Index futures change beta without selling the stock portfolio
objectives: Derive signed target-beta overlays and distinguish them from minimum-variance positions
Distinguish futures notional from economic value and margin
Price index carry with stated dividend assumptions
Assess residual, rounding, maturity and execution risks
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 2–6 carry, settlement timing, hedge variance and beta projection.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential English captions for positions 17–19; MIT forward/futures slides 25–29 inspected. Historical source specifications are not current product claims.

chapters.title: Discount factors price cash flows; a yield summarizes one price
objectives: Derive spot and forward quotations from discount factors
Prove and compute positive-cash-flow yield uniqueness
Explain why YTM does not identify a curve or average linearly
Separate internal rate from realized reinvested wealth
chapters.prerequisites: Dated present values from Chapter 2; monotone functions, logarithms and elementary differentiation.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential captions for positions 20–21; selected MIT fixed-income text and TreasuryDirect bill-pricing passage inspected; source and synthetic arithmetic independently executed.

chapters.title: Duration cancels a first derivative, not every interest-rate risk
objectives: Derive duration, convexity and correctly scaled DV01
Quantify Taylor approximation errors
Derive the duration-horizon immunization condition
Diagnose nonparallel curve risk after duration matching
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 8 cash-flow valuation and yield conventions; two derivatives and Taylor expansion.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential English captions for positions 22–23 and selected MIT fixed-income text slides 35–43. Fixed-cash-flow sensitivities and synthetic immunization examples independently executed.

chapters.title: Short-rate futures: a quotation is not a cash price
objectives: Convert a discount yield into bill price and investment yield without mixing units
Separate the futures delivery date from the underlying bill's maturity
Derive quote sensitivity and the sign of a short-rate futures hedge
Distinguish a forward-style terminal sketch from daily settled futures cash flows
chapters.prerequisites: Discount factors and forward replication from chapters 02 and 08; yield sensitivity from chapter 09; futures settlement from chapter 03.
chapters.source_scope: Full English caption text for playlist positions 24 and 25 read sequentially. Historical product details are identified as source context; synthetic examples independently reconstruct the mechanics. No comprehensive audiovisual audit.

chapters.title: Rate hedges: carry, basis, settlement timing, and accrued interest
objectives: Separate predictable bill carry from an unanticipated yield shock
Derive a rate hedge count with consistent price sensitivities and an ex ante projection coefficient
Explain deterministic-rate tailing through a complete dated settlement argument
Distinguish historical Eurodollar teaching from SOFR and clean quotation from dirty cash price
chapters.prerequisites: Bill quote and yield conventions from chapter 10; covariance projection from chapter 05; discount factors and futures marking to market.
chapters.source_scope: Full English captions for positions 26–28 read sequentially. Historical quotation language, discount-versus-simple-rate differences, and accrued-interest conventions are qualified. Synthetic arithmetic and proofs are independently constructed; no comprehensive audiovisual audit.

chapters.title: Bond futures: conversion factors, delivery choice, and rate sensitivity
objectives: Build a delivery invoice with consistent face, quote, conversion-factor and accrued-interest units
Explain why conversion factors do not make all eligible bonds economically identical
Derive a bond-forward quotation from dirty cash prices and intervening coupons
Size a first-order Treasury futures hedge using the cheapest-to-deliver sensitivity and state its limits
chapters.prerequisites: Bond cash-flow valuation and duration from chapters 08–09; cash-and-carry from chapter 02; clean and dirty prices from chapter 11.
chapters.source_scope: Full English captions for positions 29 and 30 read sequentially. Historical delivery/rounding rules are not generalized to all current products. Official CME conversion and delivery descriptions checked; numerical cases and simplified conversion calculations independently constructed.

chapters.title: Option cash flows and put–call parity
objectives: Derive all four elementary option payoffs and funded profit thresholds
Distinguish moneyness, immediate-exercise amount and a European option's price
Prove European put–call parity through statewise and dated cash-flow identities
Construct parity arbitrage ledgers and incorporate known dividends and execution frictions
chapters.prerequisites: Dated cash-flow conventions, short selling and no-arbitrage from chapters 01–02; discount factors from chapter 08.
chapters.source_scope: Full English captions for positions 31 and 61 read sequentially. Position 61 is the official put–call-parity lecture placed after basic options in the course catalog. Original finite constructions supplement the source; exercise, funding, and stock-domain assumptions are explicit.

chapters.title: Option bounds and the decision to exercise
objectives: Derive European option bounds by dated portfolio dominance
Build the prepaid-share replication for a deterministic proportional dividend yield
Prove the nondividend American-call result with its rate condition
Calculate early-exercise decisions from continuation values and derive American parity inequalities
chapters.prerequisites: European put–call parity and funded option payoffs from chapter 13; discount factors and replication from chapters 02 and 08.
chapters.source_scope: Complete English captions for positions 32–33 read sequentially. Weak bounds, rate and dividend assumptions, and model-based continuation values are made explicit. The finite exercise tree is an original pedagogical construction, developed further in chapter 18.

chapters.title: Static option strategies as piecewise-linear cash flows
objectives: Construct funded profits from signed stock, call, put, and cash positions
Derive strategy limits and break-evens from strike partitions rather than memorized diagrams
Prove vertical-spread, butterfly, and box identities and their price restrictions
Separate a calendar position's interim value from a common-expiry terminal payoff
chapters.prerequisites: Funded payoff conventions and European parity from chapter 13; bounds and exercise rights from chapter 14.
chapters.source_scope: Full English captions for positions 34–36 read sequentially. Dated American dividend inequalities complete the opening source topic; strategy analysis uses explicit European common-expiry assumptions. Original synthetic examples and a computed payoff atlas replace ambiguous premium signs and calendar heuristics.

chapters.title: From random walks to Brownian risk factors
objectives: Distinguish a process law from its one-time distributions and identify a sufficient Markov state
Derive the square-root time scaling of a finite random walk and its limiting Gaussian endpoint
Specify Brownian motion through its increments and path regularity
Derive a diffusion equation as a continuum consistency limit without claiming an unproved path-convergence theorem
chapters.prerequisites: Probability, conditional probability, means and variances, and elementary Taylor expansion. Chapter 1's distinction between payoff scenarios and probability assignments.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential reading of official English captions for playlist positions 37–39. Formal definitions, examples, convergence qualifications, and numerical certificates are original expansions; no comprehensive audiovisual audit.

chapters.title: Itô calculus, lognormal prices, and the meaning of a risk probability
objectives: Solve the Brownian density equation and state the conditions behind a central limit argument
Derive quadratic variation and the correction to the ordinary chain rule
Solve geometric Brownian motion and derive its density, moments, and return conventions
Separate an endpoint loss probability from the probability of crossing a liquidity boundary
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 16's Brownian increments, covariance, and diffusion equation; Taylor expansion, integration by parts, and Gaussian probability.
chapters.source_scope: All official English captions at playlist positions 40–43 read sequentially. Equations reconstructed; no comprehensive audiovisual audit. Quadratic-variation and endpoint-versus-hitting corrections are explicit.

chapters.title: Binomial replication and risk-neutral valuation
objectives: Derive the strict no-arbitrage interval and replicate every two-state payoff
Interpret pricing probabilities without imposing risk-neutral investor preferences
Verify dynamic self-financing and exercise-date backward induction
Identify failure of uniqueness and recombination when spanning or state sufficiency fails
chapters.prerequisites: Option payoffs and exercise styles; financing conventions; elementary linear algebra and conditional expectation.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential reading of official English captions at positions 44–45; source put independently recomputed. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Risk-neutral-preference rhetoric, interior-strike restriction, and coarse exercise-grid limitations are corrected explicitly.

chapters.title: Measure change, dynamic replication, and the Black–Scholes model
objectives: Construct and verify the constant-coefficient likelihood ratio and Brownian shift
Derive the Black–Scholes PDE from a specified self-financing portfolio
Derive call and put prices and distinguish pricing probabilities, delta, and conditional means
State the completeness, dividend, and model-risk boundaries of the replication argument
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 17–18: Itô calculus, GBM, pricing measures, and finite-state self-financing; Gaussian integration.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions at positions 46–48 read sequentially; numerical examples independently recomputed. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Conditional/truncated expectation, variance under measure change, financing, and boundary-condition corrections are explicit.

chapters.title: Solving the pricing PDE and measuring local exposure
objectives: Transform the Black–Scholes terminal PDE into an initial heat equation and evaluate its kernel integral
Derive yield-adjusted Greeks with explicit time, decimal-parameter, and contract-multiplier units
Verify parity sensitivities and limiting behavior
Distinguish local neutrality and partial derivatives from finite market-scenario changes
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 17–19: Gaussian kernel, Black–Scholes PDE and formula, self-financing; multivariable differentiation and Taylor expansion.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions at positions 49–50 read sequentially. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Kernel uniqueness, time conventions, maturity sensitivity, strategy-neutrality labels, and financed condor profit are qualified; analytic Greek derivations anticipate the next recordings.

chapters.title: Greek hedges, financing, and the cost of convexity
objectives: Solve signed delta–gamma–vega hedge systems and diagnose rank and conditioning
Derive the financed gamma–theta tradeoff and audit complete discrete hedge P&L
Separate empirical joint scenarios from independent sensitivity neutrality
Correct the distinction between forward-quote and contract-value deltas and specify the swap cash-flow bridge
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 19–20: self-financing diffusion replication, Greek formulas and units; Chapter 2 forward valuation; elementary matrix rank.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions at positions 51–54 read sequentially. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Complete-ledger gamma examples, common-expiry gamma–vega rank constraints, conditional scenario claims, forward value/quote corrections, and historical LIBOR boundary are explicit.

chapters.title: FRAs and interest-rate swaps as dated cash flows
objectives: Replicate advance-settled and end-settled FRAs with correct signs and dates
Derive par swap rates, off-market values, and discount-factor bootstraps
Value a floating bond between resets and reconcile swap bond/coupon-strip methods
Identify projection, discounting, overnight observation, and comparative-funding limitations
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 1 swap cash-flow definitions; Chapter 8 discount factors, zero and forward rates; Chapters 11 and 21 historical benchmark boundaries; dated present-value calculations.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions at positions 55–57 read sequentially, all source examples independently recomputed. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Forward-realization assumptions, FRA settlement timing, contractual reset rights, day counts, and single-curve shortcuts are explicitly qualified.

chapters.title: Currency swaps, loss quantiles, and tail risk
objectives: Reconcile domestic-valued currency legs and forward-converted cash-flow valuation with explicit units
Construct and index synchronized historical loss scenarios
Derive Gaussian VaR with drift and horizon qualifications
Compute expected shortfall with probability atoms and exhibit VaR aggregation failure
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 2 and 22 discounting, currency forward parity and swap legs; Gaussian distributions, covariance and quantiles.
chapters.source_scope: Full official English captions at positions 58–59 read sequentially. No comprehensive audiovisual audit. Source principal mismatch, pricing-versus-risk probabilities, lower empirical quantile indexing, nonmaximum VaR interpretation, and square-root scaling limits are explicit. ES and discrete counterexamples are added enrichment.

chapters.title: Portfolio risk: covariance, nonlinear losses, and evidence beyond VaR
objectives: Compute signed covariance and duration VaR with explicit units and horizon assumptions
Reconstruct cash-flow mapping and diagnose PCA portfolio-risk truncation
Compare delta/gamma approximations with full option and bond repricing
Calculate atomic expected shortfall and assess exception-count and stress evidence
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 23 loss quantiles and expected shortfall; Chapters 6 and 9 covariance and duration; Chapters 19–21 option values and Greeks; finite probability distributions and matrix eigenvectors.
chapters.source_scope: Full sequential normalized English captions at position 60 read. Source bond/mapping/PCA/option examples independently recomputed; missing exact FX discount inputs replaced by explicit synthetic data. Selected NIST PCA and historical BCBS backtesting passages inspected. No comprehensive audiovisual audit or empirical risk calibration.
